newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue downtrend in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue downtrend in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares continued their downtrend on Tuesday in below-average trade, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) report showed.
The CMA's all-share index shed 1.64 points to 346.73, its lowest since January 21. Turnover was 38.7 million pounds ($11.4 million).
"The market turns dry as there are no shares available to buy but prices are going down," Mohammad Abdullah, Intercapital managing director, told Reuters.
"Small (individual) investors are being replaced by institutional investors," Abdullah said.
Egyptian Financial and Industrial was active on the day, but ended up a fraction 0.01 pounds at 198.
"EFI was affected by good news last week," Abdullah said, referring to a report by London-based stockbrokers T. Hoare and Co.

The brokerage firm said that the privatised fertiliser firm was started with a "strong buy" rating. The Egyptian state sold 65 percent of EFI's total 3.25 million shares to private investors last year.
It said EFI's expansion plans would make it the world's largest producer of Single Super Phosphate fertiliser by 1999. "There is more to come for the firm,"
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the most active share. The stock went up only 0.50 pounds to end at 85.75, when equity worth 3.8 million pounds were traded.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 466.95 points from 477.08 points on Monday but that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 258.57 from 257.65.
Of the 94 shares traded, 29 rose, 36 fell while 29 ended unchanged.
